high.title: Fed Maintains Interest Rates at Highest Level in Over 3 Decades, Officials Show Rare Division
high.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted to keep the federal funds rate in the 3.5%-3.75% range, as widely expected by markets with 100% probability. However, the meeting revealed significant internal division with an 8-4 voting split, the strongest dissent in decades - the last time 4 FOMC members opposed was October 1992. Fed Governor Stephen Miran continued opposing the decision and called for an additional 0.25% cut to support labor markets. Three other dissenting votes came from Fed Presidents Beth Hammack (Cleveland), Neel Kashkari (Minneapolis), and Lorie Logan (Dallas), who favored more aggressive tightening. This unprecedented division signals growing uncertainty about Fed policy direction amid conflicting economic signals, which could impact global capital flows and VND stability as Vietnam remains sensitive to US monetary policy changes.

high.title: Trump Issues Hardline Warning to Iran, Oil Prices Surge Immediately
high.summary: President Trump delivered a stern warning to Iran amid escalating Middle East tensions and stalled Washington-Tehran negotiations. In a Truth Social post on April 29, Trump stated Iran "cannot stabilize the situation" and urged Tehran to change its position immediately, saying "Iran doesn't know how to sign a nuclear deal. They should be wiser immediately." Oil markets reacted instantly with WTI crude rising nearly 3% to over $103/barrel and Brent climbing about 3% above $114/barrel. Trump's post included an AI-generated image showing him with weapons and explosions with text "NO MORE MR. NICE GUY!" indicating a harder White House stance. This escalation threatens to keep oil prices elevated, potentially pushing Vietnam's 2026 inflation toward the 4-4.5% range, limiting SBV's monetary policy flexibility and maintaining pressure on the VND exchange rate.

high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Proposes Amendments to Most Important Banking Circular
high.summary: The SBV has proposed significant changes to banking regulations, notably shifting from the loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR) to a credit-to-deposit ratio (CDR). The new CDR will be calculated based on total outstanding credit and total mobilized funds rather than just loans and deposits, maintaining existing components including corporate bond investments and off-balance sheet commitments. A key adjustment involves State Treasury deposits, where the proportion counted toward funding sources will be recalculated following the established roadmap that gradually reduces and eliminates time deposits from Treasury by 2026. This regulatory change could significantly impact bank lending capacity and liquidity management, potentially affecting credit growth and banking sector profitability. The new framework may also influence government bond demand as banks adjust their asset allocation strategies under the revised requirements.

medium.title: Experts Warn Stock Market Usually Has 2 Major Downturns Each Year: Will Old Scenario Repeat?
medium.summary: Vietnamese stock market faces complex macro pressures from global oil prices and internal stress with VN-Index heavily dependent on single stock groups amid peak margin debt. Oil prices above $105/barrel from Hormuz Strait tensions could push Vietnam's 2026 inflation to 4-4.5%, limiting SBV's monetary policy room despite efforts to reduce interest rates.

medium.title: Volatility Expected to Emerge, Securities Firm Identifies Stock Groups That Could "Attract Money" After Holiday
medium.summary: VN-Index recovered for the 5th consecutive week, the longest gaining streak since late last year. MB Securities notes VN-Index completed a 200-point recovery since conflict outbreak, approaching historic highs around 1,900 points. However, internal picture shows clear divergence with money concentrated in large-cap stocks while most sectors haven't recovered proportionally.

medium.title: Securities Companies Earn Nearly 10,000 Billion VND Pre-tax Profit in First Quarter: "Crown" Changes Hands, One Name Loses Nearly 60% of Profit
medium.summary: Securities industry's total pre-tax profit in Q1/2026 reached approximately 9,700 billion VND, up 26% YoY but down 19% from Q4/2025. This marks the second consecutive quarter of declining profits from the record 19,000 billion VND peak in Q3/2025, reflecting market cooling after the boom period.

medium.title: Comprehensive Banking Profit Q1/2026: Champion Officially Revealed
medium.summary: Total profit of 27 banks reached over 94 trillion VND, up 14% YoY. Vietcombank maintains profit leadership with 11,803 billion VND (+9%), while VietinBank closes gap at 11,139 billion VND (+63%). Top 5 include Vietcombank, VietinBank, MB, Techcombank, and BIDV. Highest growth rates came from smaller banks: ABBank (+261%), PGBank (+187%), and BVBank (+169%).

medium.title: Banks Continue Strong Capital Injection into Real Estate Business: Growth 8 Times Faster Than Average, Bank Leaders Say This Sector Still Has Much Potential
medium.summary: Real estate credit outstanding reached over 2.2 trillion VND by end-February 2026, up 11.7% from Q4/2025 and 43% YoY. This growth rate is 8 times higher than the 1.4% average credit growth for the economy in the first two months of 2026, indicating strong banking sector appetite for real estate lending.

medium.title: Gold Ring and Bar Prices Evening April 28: Simultaneous Decline
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices fell sharply by 1.3-1.8 million VND per tael across major brands at 3:20 PM April 28. SJC, PNJ, DOJI gold bars and rings dropped to 164.5-167.5 million VND per tael range. International gold spot prices declined 1.3% to $4,621/ounce following previous day's 0.6% drop amid US-Iran negotiation concerns.
